catalog.callRule: needs-key: the endpoint exists and answers OpenAI-compatible requests, but every request is paid and signed, so the site never calls it and never takes a key; none: there is no endpoint to call
directories: gonka/<slug>.t27 (FAMILY model: one card per model in the chain's models_all)
trinet/<slug>.t27 (FAMILY host-class: one card per device class our network would pay $TRI for)
catalog.fieldSourceRule: a model card copies the chain: MODEL_ID, HF_COMMIT, VRAM_GB (v_ram), THROUGHPUT_PER_NONCE, VALIDATION_PERMILLE (validation_threshold x 1000) and UNITS_OF_COMPUTE_PER_TOKEN from models_all; CONTEXT_TOKENS from the --max-model-len in its model_args; POC_MODEL and POC_WEIGHT_SCALE_E4 (weight_scale_factor x 10000) from params.poc_params.models; HOSTS from the count of active participants of EPOCH whose models list names MODEL_ID; PRICE_PER_TOKEN from /v1/governance/pricing
catalog.idRule: ID is the path under specs/providers without .t27, for example gonka/minimax-m2-7; the module is provider_<ID with every non-alphanumeric run replaced by _>
catalog.statusRule: serving: on chain and at least one host of EPOCH serves it; listed: on chain, no host serves it; measured: our hardware, with a bench record a reader can rerun; planned: no code and no record, a design only
catalog.witnessRule: chain-read: copied from a public chain endpoint on CHECKED; bench-measured: a record of runs on our boards, named in SOURCES; design-only: nothing has run. A design never claims a measurement

fields.DEVICE: Xilinx Artix-7 XC7A200T. TRI-NET ran on three Alinx AX7203 boards (IDCODE 0x13636093); the t27 bench is three QMTech Wukong V1 boards (IDCODE 0x03636093), the same die
GAPS: the node keys are not on any host: no receipt from the three boards can be verified until they are re-keyed (ternary_hw_verification.t27 KEYS_NOT_ON_THIS_HOST)
nobody buys ternary compute: settlement_law.t27 EFFICIENCY_IS_NOT_DEMAND is resolved false and WHO_BUYS_TERNARY_COMPUTE is open
$TRI is on no mainnet: the site's jetton is on TON testnet
the UART, not the cell, bounds throughput; a faster transport is not built
fields.GONKA_PARALLEL: Gonka's Proof of Compute v2 races seeded transformer forward passes and accepts a host within a distance threshold by a binomial test; 20% of a host's weight needs no collateral and 20% of collateral is slashed for invalid work. Here the job is integer, so acceptance is equality and needs no threshold; stake and slash play the part of collateral
MEASURED: TRINET MAC32, a 32-wide balanced-ternary dot product computed as popcount(agreements) - popcount(disagreements), bit-exact on the board: 512/512 (ternary_hw_verification.t27)
6400/6400 jobs on each of three nodes at their own baud window centres, zero failures (ternary_hw_verification.t27)
over the UART transport no node can exceed about 4770 jobs/s, against a compute ceiling about 480 times higher (TRI_NET_HANDOFF.md)
fields.NAME: Artix-7 XC7A200T FPGA host
fields.NOTE: Gonka has no FPGA path at all: its hosts run vLLM on GPUs and its proof races transformer forward passes. An FPGA earns on TRI-NET only through jobs written for the FPGA cell, which today means the 32-wide ternary dot product.
fields.PROOF: bit-exact recompute: a job is 24 bytes, the answer 19 bytes carrying the node id and a tag; the verifier recomputes the 32-wide balanced-ternary dot product and credits only an identical answer (settlement_law.t27, AUDIT_RATE_PERCENT 100: every job is checked while the network is small)
fields.REWARD: 1 mTRI per accepted job (REWARD_PER_JOB_MTRI 1, 1000 mTRI = 1 TRI), minted when the verifier accepts the job; nothing is minted for a job nobody checked
fields.STAKE: 1000 mTRI minimum stake (MIN_STAKE_MTRI), 200 mTRI slashed per bad receipt (SLASH_PER_BAD_RECEIPT_MTRI); a damaged receipt is neither credited nor slashed
fields.SUMMARY_EN: An FPGA board its owner rents out to TRI-NET for $TRI. The board computes balanced-ternary dot products bit-exactly, so a job is checked by recomputing it and comparing for equality, not by a statistical test. Measured on three boards; nobody buys this compute yet.
fields.TOKEN: $TRI: cap 3^21 = 10460353203, all of it mined on accepted work, no pre-mine and no sale (settlement_law.t27); issued on TON and Solana by owner decision 2026-09-24; today only a TON testnet jetton exists (gHashTag/trinity apps/website/src/lib/triToken.ts, TRI_NETWORK testnet)

fields.GONKA_PARALLEL: Gonka admitted consumer cards from 2025-11-05 (gonka-docs 3480cc7382, 40 GB minimum across the cards of one node) and stopped on 2026-06-05 (gonka-docs ff70a0f856); the models it serves on 2026-10-03 need 280 to 560 GB per host. The class Gonka left behind is the class TRI-NET would serve
fields.NAME: Consumer GPU host (24 GB)
fields.NOTE: Market rent for this class, from our own bills: RTX 4090 at 0.34 USD (community) to 0.74 USD (secure) per GPU-hour on RunPod (igla-coder-gpu LEDGER.md). A $TRI reward only competes with that once $TRI has a market price, which it does not have.
fields.PROOF: design: deterministic integer or ternary kernels whose answer is identical on any card, checked by recomputing a sample on a second host and credited only on equality, the FPGA rule carried over; a floating-point job would need Gonka-style statistical acceptance with its own threshold per device class
fields.REWARD: design: the FPGA law, mTRI per accepted job minted on acceptance, scaled by a per-class weight factor (Gonka's weight_scale_factor per model) so that one device class cannot drown another
fields.STAKE: design: the FPGA law, 1000 mTRI minimum stake and 200 mTRI slashed per bad receipt (settlement_law.t27); not in force for GPUs
fields.SUMMARY_EN: A gaming GPU its owner would rent out to TRI-NET for $TRI. Gonka no longer admits a card like this: a Gonka ML node now needs about 320 GB of GPU memory, fourteen of these cards. TRI-NET could take one card at a time, with jobs that fit it and are checked by recomputation. Nothing is built yet.

fields.CONFLICT: the owner decided $TRI lives on TON and Solana; GNK lives on the Gonka chain and, wrapped, on Ethereum. No chain holds both, so every route either puts $TRI on a chain not chosen for it or needs a bridge nobody has built. Before any route, $TRI needs a mainnet issue: a testnet jetton cannot be paired
IBC_CHANNELS: channel-1 Osmosis (no GNK on Osmosis on CHECKED)
PARALLELS: who pays: Gonka pays its hosts almost entirely by issuance, its subsidies were about 100000 times its fees on CHECKED; TRI-NET mints on accepted jobs, so both pay for work before anyone buys it, and both wait on demand (settlement_law.t27 WHO_BUYS_TERNARY_COMPUTE)

proof: Gonka's Proof of Compute v2 is statistical, seeded forward passes accepted within a distance threshold by a binomial test; TRI-NET's is exact, a bit-identical recompute, which is cheaper to check and works only for integer jobs
entry: a Gonka host needs 280 to 560 GB of GPU memory on CHECKED, so one 24 GB card is out; TRI-NET would take one card or one FPGA board
weight: Gonka scales the PoC weight of each model (weight_scale_factor) so that one model cannot crowd out another; TRI-NET would need the same per device class
collateral: Gonka gives 20% of a host's weight without collateral and slashes 20% for invalid work and 10% for downtime; TRI-NET asks a 1000 mTRI stake and slashes 200 mTRI per bad receipt
vesting: Gonka vests rewards over 180 epochs, about 171 days at the measured epoch; TRI-NET has no vesting
admission: Gonka's allowlist ended at height 2475000 and anyone may register a host; TRI-NET has three boards and no public registration
ROUTES: ethereum-uniswap: issue $TRI as an ERC-20 on Ethereum and open a TRI/WGNK pool on Uniswap v3 beside the WGNK/USDT pool; needs nobody's permission, and puts $TRI on a chain the owner did not choose

gonka-pool: bring $TRI to the Gonka chain (an Ethereum ERC-20 through the Gonka bridge, or an IBC denom) and win a Gonka governance vote approving it for trade (MsgApproveBridgeTokenForTrading or MsgApproveIbcTokenForTrading); the chain's singleton pool is not registered yet and the approved list holds only USDC and USDT
osmosis-ibc: send GNK to Osmosis over IBC channel-1 and pair it there with $TRI as an Osmosis tokenfactory denom; needs nobody's permission, puts $TRI on a third chain, and Osmosis holds no GNK today
ton-or-solana: pair on the chains $TRI was decided for, on a TON or Solana exchange; needs GNK carried to TON or Solana, and the Gonka bridge serves only Ethereum
